body:
In [5.3.1](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x14-V5-File-Handling.md#v53-file-storage) "public folder" term used
> Verify that files uploaded or generated by untrusted input which are stored in a **public folder**, are not executed as server-side program code when accessed directly with an HTTP request 

Potentially, such location may not always be "public"...
Should it better to put something like "separate folder" instead?
Or just clarify the description to focus on untrusted content, and not mention the location itself? 
And it could be that number of different folders are used for such uploaded/generated files (e.g. due to different user flows or functional parts of application)...

comments.body:
I do not like the term “public folder” either. I suggest we just drop it and go with…
> Verify that files uploaded or generated by untrusted input are not executed program code
> 
… because there are so many situations where uploaded files can be executed in various other situations. As is, public folder is rather limiting in this requirement and only describes one specific situation. But I‘ve been shot down several times with my suggestions. I am glad to see that other people recognize the weakness of this requirement as is.
I changed it 2 days ago, please read rationale here first: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1087#issuecomment-2777592562

Example situation: user can upload a file into *public folder* where it is accessible with *direct HTTP request* and due to web server configuration to handle such files as program codes, it will be executed as program code. Classical PHP application issue, but not limited to PHP.

If we remove *public folder*, then how do you access it with a direct HTTP request? Maybe there can be some mapping included, but effectively it is a public folder. If we remove "public folder", I think it causes more confusion.

If you are going to manipulate the application program code to load this uploaded file as program code, it is a separate problem and covered by 5.3.2.

> As is, public folder is rather limiting in this requirement and only describes one specific situation.

This precisely focuses on this attack vector and nothing else. If there are uncovered scenarios, then please raise them as a separate topic or issue.

@oleksiidov - does it clarify the point for the requirement for you?

@elarlang thank you for the link on previous discussion and for explanation what is the case behind of the requirement description.  
And I got what slightly confused me... 

What do you think if we change wording a little, just avoid confusion with "input which"?
From
> Verify that files uploaded or generated by untrusted input **which are** stored in a public folder, are not executed as server-side program code when accessed directly with an HTTP request.

to
> Verify that files uploaded or generated by untrusted input **and** stored in a public folder are not executed as server-side program code when accessed directly with an HTTP request.

> Verify that files uploaded or generated by untrusted input and stored in a public folder are not executed as server-side program code when accessed directly with an HTTP request.

I'm ok with that, PR it in.
